entries.result: Lemma l:2, energy of a trimmed low-energy state
entries.title: Energy bound after trimming at one cut
entries.summary: The printed proof drops two terms, one of which depends on 1/ε; the bound ε<sub>0</sub> + 6√δ and the constant chosen from it downstream have not yet been rechecked.
entries.context: Lemma l:2 trims a low-energy state to the constant Schmidt rank Bδ at one cut and bounds the energy of the result. The algorithm uses it to show that a good state of constant rank at a cut always exists, and chooses its accuracy constant cε = (ε/169)2 from this bound.
entries.claims: If δ(1 + 1/ε) ≤ 1/2 and w has energy at most ε0 + δ, the normalized trimmed state has energy at most ε0 + 6√δ.
entries.found: The proof first bounds the change in one local term by 2√δ′ with δ′ = δ(1 + 1/ε) ≥ δ, then continues with 2√δ; and of a term (1 − ε<sub>0</sub>)δ′ it keeps only −ε<sub>0</sub>δ′. Keeping both gives a bound of the form ε<sub>0</sub> + 2(δ + δ′ + 2√δ′), which depends on 1/ε. This reading comes from the tracking issue and has not yet been written up as a note.
entries.impact: Probably not. A smaller choice of cε, polynomial in ε, appears to restore the later inequality 14√cε < ε/12, which would change constants but not the polynomial running time.
entries.plan: Write the paper-gap note with the corrected bound, recheck the choice of cε and the inequality used in the proof of Lemma l:leading, and record whether only constants change.
